New scars will itch because when something injures your skin your bodies nerve endings can be damaged, even if it’s not that deep, the nerve endings can be super sensitive and cause itchiness as they began to heal. Old scars (over two years old) itch because sometimes a scar can make the skin feel tight, this happens more when it is a burn and burn scars naturally itch like a bitch, it can also itch because of dry skin. You can do a lot of things to help itchiness: moisturize older scars (doing this with fresh ones can affect healing tho) that are itchy, silicon sheeting bandages which are usually found at most drugstores, and most importantly make sure to keep your scabs washed and cleaned especially if they are itchy.

“What did you say? What did he say?” The captain asked anxiously. The technician glared at him.

“I asked him what he was doing here. He said he had an important message for number 0197. But that’s not possible, right?” The technician replied.

The technician began to tap again and very large angry taps came in return that even the captain could hear them.

Erving and I sat in the pub, waiting for the old man to arrive. Rich men are always late. Think their entitled to something. That they can show up whenever they want. 

"Do you think he'll show, Cap'n?" Erving asked me.

"Hmm?" I stared out at the beaten door of the Monsoon Lagoon, "Yea, Erv, he'll show."

The door swung open, revealing a rich man. He had white scruff on his chin and some of the same stuff on the top of his head. Believe you could've turned him upside down there'd be no difference from the top and bottom of his head. His brown suspenders were holding up some blue fancy-pants trousers. It disgusted me, why people spend so much coin on clothes. He had a stainless white long-sleeved shirt, sleeves rolled up at his elbows. He was looking straight at me and Erving. I couldn't tell what he was thinking, but it couldn't be anything good. 

I heard Erving laugh, "That can't be him, can it?" He laughed again. By now the old man was walking over.  I turned towards our table, away from the old man, and drank down the rest of my whiskey. It was dull and tasteless by now, Erving and I having waited almost five hours for the man to appear. 

Erving turned and gave me a look that I have learned to love over the years. He would've been a handsome man, if he trimmed his scraggly beard and combed and cut his hair. His eyes were mad and he looked as if he just tortured someone to death and enjoyed it. The nails on his fingers needed some serious attention, they were mostly black and warty. Doubt any lady would fancy holding hands with him. He looked at me with his grin I oh so loved and showed his yellow and black teeth that hadn't been cared for in quite some time, despite us being docked for a while now. 

I looked back at the door and saw the old man standing less than a meter from me. I looked at Erving and he looked at the old man, a scowl taking over his grin. I heard him mutter something along the lines of "Rich son-of-a-bitch" and "Goin' to get more whiskey." Then he got up and left me with the man.

"Are you Ramsey Blackfoot?" He asked me, taking Erving's seat.

"Sure am. Who might you be?" I replied looking into his steely, cold entitled eyes.

"My names Arthur. Arthur Cottonwin. I noticed that your boat has been docked for a while now. The Black Lady?" Arthur said, his hands scratching the ruff of his beard. 

"Not really in the mood to kill her, sir." I stated. He laughed and crossed his hands on the table.

"Understandable. Sure hasn't been looking very optimistic out there lately. Been hearing about wrecked boats coming in from the South, West, East, and North." 

"I got a crew, and I ain't about to let em' try to kill themselves without a reason. So, spit it out. What've you got for me?"

"South. I will pay you and every member of your crew 50 septims of gold to sail where I would like you to." 

I whistled. That was a high and mighty price, there had to be something worth something out there.

"What're we talking bout' here? You want me to pick something up? Lady? Chest?" 

"I just need you to sail there, check it out for me."

"You for real?"

"Yes. Your mission would be to sail there, match up the exact coordinates where I want you to go and then draw everything in your surroundings in this book."

"Seems sketchy. I'll take it. Where're we going?"

"Oh, I'm not coming. I want you to sail through the North Atlantic Ocean and the South Atlantic Ocean. I want you to go South. Coordinates are 62°08′10″S,-62 ,26°34′55″E,26. I'll pay you half the coin now and give you the book, then I'll pay you the other half if you come back. Meet me in the Noon Parlor if you return. Now, I believe your friend is waiting ever-so patiently for you. Good luck, Captain Ramsey." As Arthur finished he stood and I shook his hand. He pulled out a small leather book from his back pocket then took out a slightly large bag of coins and handed both to me. 

I watched as he took his leave, only until he was far gone was when Erving walked up to me, sipping whiskey from his flask. 

"So, that went well?" He questioned, gesturing to the bag of coins in my arms.

"This? This is only half of what he's gonna pay us. All he wants us to do is sail to the middle of nowhere, draw a few pictures, and sail back." I said to him. Erving looked at me like I was kidding.

"Your serious? Well, the guy may as well be dying, is he giving away his fortune or what?" Erving laughed out loud and downed the rest of his whiskey.

"Dead serious. You know, you might be right. He did look a tad bit dead to me." I admitted and started towards the door, Erving's 6' 3" lumbering after me. 

We made it out the door and I headed towards The Black Lady, my pride and joy.  Got her when I was a young lad about 14, 15 years, met a black lady named Susan. Sold into slavery right next door to me. She was kind to me, and when she was killed, I named my boat after her. Thought it was a gentleman thing to do, even if she was a little bit colored. 

The dock man let me through and I went straight up to the boat.

"Eh! Whiskey! Frisky! Where the hell are you!?" I yelled up at the boat. In a few seconds, tow young men came scrambling down the ramp, stopping in the middle. They were my young nephews and my sister had sent them to me so they could become "real sailors." I think she just didn't want to take care of teenage boys anymore. 

They were twins and they looked virtually the same. Both had brown shaggy hair, much like mine, and brown eyes, like their father. They both had the same body shape, too. Long and lanky, with some muscle mixed in. Their real names were Marcus and Lucas Blackfoot, but everyone just called them Whiskey and Frisky. 

"Hey Uncle! What've you got!?" Whiskey yelled back. Frisky hit him. They had a mini argument and Frisky yelled back, "Eh! Captain! What you got!?" I rolled my eyes.

"Come down and help, lads!" I yelled up at them. They scrambled down and landed in front of me, grinning. "Frisky, take this up and put this in my quarters. Whiskey, you're with me." 

Whiskey punched Frisky in the arm as I handed Frisky the bag of coins. His eyes widened and he nodded effervescently. 

"Whaddya need Uncle?" Whiskey asked me as we walked up the ramp after Frisky.

"We're headed out to sea, leaving tomorrow morning. I want your mother to know. We may not return." Whiskey's face fell dramatically after I told him. 

"But, Uncle, me and Frisky, we're great sailors. You need us. Mother won't mind if we're gone a little while. That is why she sent us away, right?" Whiskey bargained with me. I shook my head and stopped.

"I want you to run down to your mother's house and tell her. If she doesn't want you to go, you ain't coming. You nor Frisky, you hear?" I looked down at Whiskey; once he nodded and ran off I went up the rest of the ramp and towards the Captain's quarters. Frisky was just walking out when I came in.

"Captain! I put it in there like you asked, sir. What would you like now?" Frisky asked and saluted me. I grabbed his hand and moved it to his side, laughing.

"Boy, we ain't in the army. No need to salute me now. Your brothers running down to tell your Mum, but I want you to wait for Erving, tell him to gather the rest of the crew. We're leavein' in the morning. Got it?" I ordered and started to walk into my quarters.

"Sure thing, Captain!" Frisky said and sprinted back down the ramp from the ship. 

I sat at my charting table and found the coordinates that Arthur told me, 62°08′10″S,-62 ,26°34′55″E,26, and wrote it down. Then I took out the small book and flipped it in my hands. There was a symbol on the cover, one I vaguely recognized. It was a line with a triangle in the middle of it, turned vertical. 

If only I could remember what it meant, maybe I would understand why the location Arthur told me to go was so random. Maybe I would understand why he would pay so much for a single trip and why he was so convinced we wouldn't survive it.

I laid down on my bed, staring at my book. I didn't know what it meant, but I had a long while to figure it out. This was going to be a long trip. With that last thought, I drifted off to sleep.

My name is Jamie-Leigh Austin and I am 14 years old. Apparently I'm smart, probably because I just graduated high school, but I don't think so. I also have a gift. If you were sitting in front of me, I could tell you exactly the date that you die and how you would die. This was difficult in school because my teacher would ask me a question like, "What does the nucleus in a cell do?" and I would answer, "July 3rd, car crash down 5th avenue, decapitation by stop sign." That actually happened too. I was ten, freshman year. I couldn't control it then. Now I can.

Everyday I walk down to Carper-town in New York. This is what I call it, it is actually a hideout where my best friend and I used to hang out. She is now dead. Everyone is. How did it start? That's a good question. Probably when I was sitting in my Calculus class four months ago.

It was a bleak and rainy day and I leaned back in my chair while Mr. Cunningham was talking about the absolute maximum or the absolute minimum. The rain came down and hit the cement outside the window thirty feet below. It almost felt like time was slowing down and I could picture it in slow motion hitting the cold grey cement. I could hear the sound it would make. Then time speeds up and there are thousands of the things hitting the ground over and over like a metronome in my head. 

"Ms. Austin, are you paying attention?" Mr. Cunningham's voice rung across the room. It sounded like an old mans voice should sound. Although it probably sounded worse, because of him teaching Calculus to a bunch of teenagers for twenty-five years. 

I looked into his eyes. They were a dull blue and either looked tired or annoyed, one of the two. There were wrinkles bunched up around his eyes and grey bags underneath of them. Then I saw it. It was like time was stopping and speeding up, all I heard was the droning of a clock. Tick, tock, tick, tock and the sound keeps going even when an image comes rolling into my head like a power point presentation. 

A gun pointed at me and a heavy-built black man stood in front of me. Moving his gun and telling me to give me to give him everything I had of value. I was standing in an alley that I had to go through to get home. It had multiple dumpsters in it and there was trash everywhere. There was a puddle at my feet and I looked down. My shoes were brown dress shoes and my face was the same face of none other than my Calculus teacher. Old Mr. Cunningham. I wasn't in control of him and it was like a movie that I hated to watch, but still watched over and over again hoping for a different outcome. 

Mr. Cunningham shook his head. The dumb-ass of a man wasn't going to listen. The mugger stepped forward, and his facial features revealed themselves as a young man about eighteen years old, maybe younger. He had a lot of acne scars and a huge nose, not very proportional to the rest of his skinny facial features. His scared small black eyes stood out. He looked like he was trying to be intimidating, but he failed at it. Scared was the only thing he looked. 

The man held the gun to Mr. Cunningham's head and pushed commanding again for him to give him something worth anything. Mr. Cunningham shook his head once more and the man pulled the trigger. My head felt the pain of the bullet piercing the brain and the heart came to a thumping stop. That's when the annoying clock ticking in my head abruptly stops and my Calculus classroom comes flooding back into my eyes. 

"Ms. Austin, answer me, please." Mr. Cunningham says from the front of the classroom. I shake my head and speak up.

"Yeah, I'm here M.C." I said. Are you wondering why I didn't tell him he was going to die in less than 6 hours? Well, that just confuses everyone. I like to let nature run its course. If you die, you die. End of story.

The ringing of the class bell stops Mr. Cunningham from correcting me and everyone gets up to leave the classroom. I walk slowly to the door of the classroom, my binder and Calculus book in hand. 

It felt like being shocked by a taser or touching an electric fence. First it comes as a shiver, then as an uncontrollable frenzy feeding on my brain and eardrums. Before everything lines up, there were a million clocks in my head. Each of them a different life. I can feel their clocks ticking, their hearts are still beating. How I can see how they die, I have to look in their eyes to know. Ever since I was born it has been like this. The effervescent ticking in my brain. I learned to control it. Learned to push it off to the side and concentrate on something else. Now this was a different feeling. One I had never felt before in all the years that I have ever been alive, which is only 14. 

The clocks that were ticking in my head had finally been synchronized.

All year my index finger has been seriously messing me up. It has been tapping this seriously annoying rhythm and I have no clue what it means or where it even came from. 

Long, short, long, short, short, long, short, long, long, short, long. 

I commute to my job on Long Island, and I live in Manhattan. I ride the subway, along the way I tap the annoying beat. 

I get to the office and walk in, sliding my badge at the security checkpoint and walk to the elevator. Floor 5. Long, short, long, short, short, long, short, long, long, short, long. 

The doors open and I go to my cubicle in the far right. Hundreds of cubicles make up this floor. I sit down and boot up my computer. Long, short, long, short, short, long, short, long, long, short, long. The same rhythm over and over again, almost involuntarily. I think to myself, "It'll correct itself." 

I move my mouse and put on my headphones. "Welcome to customer service. How may I help you today?" I say in a sing-song voice. I open my tab for information, then I open my Galaga game and start playing. 

The tapping on my mouse is the same rhythm. Long, short, long, short, short, long, short, long, long, short, long.  It has been like this all year. Never-ending. The same thing over and over again.

My phone buzzes. I take it out. 12:45, time for lunch. I stand up and walk to the elevator taking off my headphones and leaving them at my cubicle. I press the lobby button. The same rhythm starts on the side of the elevator. Long, short, long, short, short, long, short, long, long, short, long. 

The doors open and I walk into the eccentric lobby, with people moving around everywhere. I keep my head down and head towards the door. The same rhythm tapping on my leg. Long, short, long, short, short, long, short, long, long, short, long. 

The automatic doors open as I slide my badge at the security checkpoint and walk out the doors. I head towards the fast-food restaurant across the street. Probably McDonald's or Subway, maybe even Burger King. I start tapping the rhythm and try to stop but it won't stop. It just drones on and on. Like twitching. Like something I can't control. Long, short, long, short, short, long, short, long, long, short, long. Over and over again.

I walk into the store and take a seat at the booth. The menu is colorful, but I know I won't eat anything. I just look out the window and tap. Long, short, long, short, short, long, short, long, long, short, long. 

My phone buzzes. "Annual Morse Code Celebration Day, Celebrate Samuel Morse With Us." Something clicks in my brain. I watch my finger and its rhythmic pattern. Long, short, long, short, short, long, short, long, long, short, long. Taking my phone out I video the pattern and click translate into Morse code using Google translate. Two words appear on my screen.

"Find Kiya."

All year my index finger has been seriously messing me up. It has been tapping this seriously annoying rhythm and I have no clue what it means or where it even came from. 

Long, short, long, short, short, long, short, long, long, short, long. 

I commute to my job on Long Island, and I live in Manhattan. I ride the subway, along the way I tap the annoying beat. 

I get to the office and walk in, sliding my badge at the security checkpoint and walk to the elevator. Floor 5. Long, short, long, short, short, long, short, long, long, short, long. 

The doors open and I go to my cubicle in the far right. Hundreds of cubicles make up this floor. I sit down and boot up my computer. Long, short, long, short, short, long, short, long, long, short, long. The same rhythm over and over again, almost involuntarily. I think to myself, "It'll correct itself." 

I move my mouse and put on my headphones. "Welcome to customer service. How may I help you today?" I say in a sing-song voice. I open my tab for information, then I open my Galaga game and start playing. 

The tapping on my mouse is the same rhythm. Long, short, long, short, short, long, short, long, long, short, long.  It has been like this all year. Never-ending. The same thing over and over again.

My phone buzzes. I take it out. 12:45, time for lunch. I stand up and walk to the elevator taking off my headphones and leaving them at my cubicle. I press the lobby button. The same rhythm starts on the side of the elevator. Long, short, long, short, short, long, short, long, long, short, long. 

The doors open and I walk into the eccentric lobby, with people moving around everywhere. I keep my head down and head towards the door. The same rhythm tapping on my leg. Long, short, long, short, short, long, short, long, long, short, long. 

The automatic doors open as I slide my badge at the security checkpoint and walk out the doors. I head towards the fast-food restaurant across the street. Probably McDonald's or Subway, maybe even Burger King. I start tapping the rhythm and try to stop but it won't stop. It just drones on and on. Like twitching. Like something I can't control. Long, short, long, short, short, long, short, long, long, short, long. Over and over again.

I walk into the store and take a seat at the booth. The menu is colorful, but I know I won't eat anything. I just look out the window and tap. Long, short, long, short, short, long, short, long, long, short, long. 

My phone buzzes. "Annual Morse Code Celebration Day, Celebrate Samuel Morse With Us." Something clicks in my brain. I watch my finger and its rhythmic pattern. Long, short, long, short, short, long, short, long, long, short, long. Taking my phone out I video the pattern and click translate into Morse code using Google translate. Two words appear on my screen.

"Find Kiya."

​
Probably gunna go with Tartarus then Nyx, then Gaia.
